reason: E2 and E3 directly support the 500 °C peak hardness and wear resistance, and the recrystallization-induced softening above 500 °C, but they are on CoCrFeNiMn, not FeNiCrCoCu. E1 shows oxide formation on a different HEA (FeCoNiMnCu) at 800 °C in air, not at 500 °C in vacuum, and does not address Cu-oxide spinels or solid lubrication. The specific claim of a Cr₂O₃–Cu-oxide composite lubricating layer forming under vacuum at 500 °C on FeNiCrCoCu is not directly evidenced.
premises: Vacuum heat treatment at ~500 °C maximizes hardness in HEA coatings via a heterogeneous nanostructure
Peak hardness at 500 °C corresponds to the lowest wear rate in HEA coatings
Thermal exposure of a similar HEA coating in air forms a protective Cr₂O₃ and spinel oxide layer
Heat treatment above 500 °C causes full recrystallization, grain coarsening, and hardness loss
The FeNiCrCoCu coating can form a Cr₂O₃–Cu-oxide composite layer that acts as a solid lubricant
